item.strong: SRS v1 · Bank Customer Onboarding Application

srs.title: Bank Customer Onboarding Application
srs.summary: The system facilitates secure customer onboarding with mandatory KYC verification, supporting dual approval workflows (Onboarding Staff + Compliance Officer), and ensures persistent audit logging for regulatory compliance. It integrates with the existing Customer Management System (CMS) and enforces
assumptions: The existing Customer Management System (CMS) has defined APIs for customer data ingestion and status updates.
Compliance Officer user accounts are pre-configured with approval privileges in the application.
The secure document storage component supports storing up to 5 documents per customer profile.
Audit logs must be retained and stored securely for a minimum period of 7 years before archival processes begin.
stakeholders: Onboarding Staff: Initiate onboarding requests and perform initial verification checks.
Compliance Officer: Holds final authority to approve or reject customer onboarding after the dual-check process.
Customers: Submit KYC data and supporting documents electronically.
System Administrators: Manage user roles, system configuration, and archival scheduling.
External Regulatory Bodies (FIU-IND): Recipient of Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) if money laundering is suspected.
System Integrator: Responsible for connecting the new module with the legacy Customer Management System.

risks.title: Data Loss Risk
risks.text: If the secure storage mechanism fails to cap the number of documents at 5 or fails during the 7-year retention cycle, the bank could face regulatory penalties for over/under-retention or data loss.

risks.text: The brief specifies internal dual approval but may not explicitly address all regulatory mandates (e.g., specific document types like GST/PAN verification, risk profiling, or rejection justification).

risks.text: The requirement to integrate with an existing, unspecified Customer Management System introduces significant technical risk regarding API compatibility and data mapping.

Does the 'secure storage' requirement include strict access controls, encryption at rest/transit, and role-based access control (RBAC) as per banking standards, or is this outside the current scope?

ranking.why: high regulation with evolving requirements: iterations plus V-Model verification gates
strict verification and validation: every build phase has a matching test phase
risk-driven loops for high uncertainty or technical risk
continuous secure deployment with automated security checks
short iterations absorb frequently changing requirements
rapid prototyping for small, low-risk systems

rejected.why: rigid once a phase closes; late changes are expensive
heavy risk analysis each loop is costly when requirements are clear
its value is continuous delivery, which this project needs little of
testing comes late, so verification evidence arrives after design is locked
light documentation clashes with formal audit and sign-off
too little rigour for high-risk or regulated systems

item.text: Done. **Agile–V-Model hybrid** fits best: 6 phases, each with an exit gate tied to requirement IDs.
